experiment.hypothesis: Reducing the AdamW learning rate from 1e-3 to 5e-4 while extending the training horizon to 40 epochs will allow the ResNet-18 to converge more precisely to the validation optimum, reducing the epoch-to-epoch oscillation observed in t0001 (val accuracy fluctuated 0.994-0.996 in epochs 15-20). The lower LR provides smaller gradient steps in the final phase of training, enabling the model to settle into a sharper minimum. With patience increased to 8, the model gets more room to find improvements before early stopping triggers. This should yield a 0.1-0.3% improvement over the 99.59% baseline.

decision.rationale: The ResNet-18 (t0001) is the clear winner at 99.59-99.62% val accuracy, outperforming both transformers by 0.3-0.5%. However, it used a relatively high LR of 1e-3 for AdamW, which likely caused oscillation in later epochs (val accuracy fluctuated between 0.994-0.996 in epochs 15-20). A lower LR (5e-4) with more epochs (40) and increased early-stopping patience (8) should allow finer convergence around the optimum. The architecture (hidden=64, depth=1, dropout=0.3) is well-matched to 28x28 histopathology and should be preserved. The compact transformer (t0003) cannot be continued because its cosine schedule horizon (25 epochs) is exhausted. The multi-scale transformer underperformed and is not worth further investment. This trial isolates the LR/epoch-count variable to test whether the ResNet-18 can push past 99.6%.
